copy: A fiber label names ingredients. It cannot predict seams, friction, heat, movement—or your nervous system today.
There is no autism fabric list. The evidence asks us to respect variable first-person experience, not manufacture a stereotype.
Sensory-inclusive fashion starts by replacing material labels with encounter variables: construction, pressure, body site, duration and context. That is a design brief—not a diagnosis.
“Soft” is not a universal textile fact. A thread on why fiber ≠ fabric ≠ garment ≠ sensory experience—and what the evidence can actually support.
Your skin does not read the fiber label.
A twelve-minute object-led essay on touch, textile and sensory autonomy.
